Job Description: ​
agilon health is transforming primary care by building one of the nation's leading value-based care platforms — and our Legal team is at the center of that growth. The Associate General Counsel, Contracting supports agilon's payor contracting function by providing practical legal support across the full contract lifecycle, from initial negotiation through post-execution management.
Reporting to the Sr. Associate General Counsel, Payor Contracting, this attorney will develop and apply knowledge of Medicare Advantage contracting, value-based care arrangements, and healthcare regulatory requirements. This role is well-suited for a transactional attorney with a healthcare background who is looking to deepen their payor contracting expertise and grow within an in-house legal team that is trusted and influential within the business.

Support end-to-end negotiation of Medicare Advantage risk agreements, including financial terms, risk-bearing entity structures, DOFR allocations, and performance guarantees, in partnership with senior legal and Payor Contracting leadership.
Draft, review, and maintain payor contract templates and assist in updating template language to reflect current regulatory requirements and market conditions.
Assist with attorney-to-attorney correspondence and support escalations, disputes, and resolutions under the direction of senior counsel.
Monitor CMS regulatory developments and assist in advising business partners on contract language implications; support preparation for Joint Operating Committee (JOC) meetings, dispute notices, and other payor-facing communications.
Assist in coordinating with Finance, Contract Analysis, and other cross-functional stakeholders to align negotiated financial terms with approved financial models.
Support payor contract interpretation, post-execution management, amendments, renewals, notices, reconciliations, and other ongoing contract matters.
Vendor Contracting
Draft, review, and negotiate commercial vendor and third-party agreements, including technology, SaaS, professional services, consulting, data and analytics, clinical services, business associate, licensing, and supply agreements.
Collaborate with IT, Information Security, Privacy, Finance, Compliance, and business owners to ensure vendor agreements appropriately address business, legal, regulatory, security, and operational requirements.
Support development and maintenance of standard vendor contract templates, playbooks, and negotiation guidelines.
Additional Contracting & Cross-Functional Support
While the primary focus of this role is payor and vendor contracting, agilon's legal team operates as a collaborative enterprise function. Attorneys with experience or interest in any of the following areas will find opportunities to contribute:
Physician and partner agreements, including employee lease agreements, medical leadership agreements, reimbursement arrangements, and program incentive agreements.
ACO program contracting, including MSSP and LEAD managed care services agreements, participating provider agreements, and partner participation agreements.
Clinical program agreements, co-management arrangements, and other provider-facing contracts.
General Legal Support & Cross-Functional Partnership
Research federal and state legal developments affecting agilon's markets and contractual arrangements and provide timely analysis to senior legal staff and business stakeholders.
Assist in translating legal, regulatory, financial, and operational risks into clear, practical guidance that enables informed business decisions.
Support Legal's advisory role in risk adjustment, data sharing, and regulatory compliance matters as they intersect with contracting.
Partner effectively across Legal, Compliance, Finance, Operations, and Market teams in a highly matrixed environment.
Perform other duties and support additional projects as assigned, consistent with the evolving needs of the Legal department and the business.

At least 5 years of relevant transactional legal experience in a law firm, in-house legal department, or a combination of both.
Some experience with or exposure to healthcare payor contracting, value-based care arrangements, or similarly complex risk-based healthcare agreements.
Foundational knowledge of Value-Based Care, Medicare Advantage Organizations, and healthcare fraud and abuse laws.
Ability to draft and negotiate agreements, provide clear advice under complex situations, and build relationships across stakeholder groups.
Ability to exercise initiative, independence, and sound judgment and to work proactively with appropriate supervision.
Ability to identify and articulate legal and business risks and support balanced, informed decision-making.
Ability to work effectively across functions and within a highly matrixed organization.

Prior in-house healthcare experience, particularly in a value-based care, managed care, or payor-facing environment.

Working here means having every opportunity to achieve your goals – and to help others accomplish theirs, too. Join our team as we help shape the future.
This Staff Attorney will support our Complex Litigation Team, which is responsible for providing top-quality representation to Hartford insureds in litigated matters for some of our most complex and high-exposure product, liability, premises operations, auto, general liability and construction injury liability matters.

As an in-house, remote Staff Attorney for The Hartford , you will join a collaborative environment where you will have direct contact with our Claims Professionals while working from home!

Work on High-Exposure, Complex Matters: Join a team that handles some of Hartford’s most challenging and high-value litigation, including product liability, construction injury, premises liability, auto and general liability matters.
Sharpen Your Litigation Strategy Skills: Analyze intricate legal issues, develop case strategy, conduct extensive legal research, and draft substantive motions that have a meaningful impact on case outcomes.
Partner with Experienced Trial Attorneys: Work alongside accomplished complex litigation attorneys, gaining mentorship and hands-on experience in some of the organization’s most significant cases.
Meaningful Involvement in Trial Preparation: Participate in depositions, mediations, arbitrations, expert coordination, and trial preparation while helping build compelling case themes and defense strategies.
Flexibility Meets Innovation: Enjoy the autonomy of a remote work environment while leveraging advanced case management systems and progressive AI-enabled tools. Work from home day to day, with in-person collaboration and appearances as needed.
Comprehensive Rewards Package: Benefit from competitive medical, dental, vision, life insurance, a 401(k) with company match, annual incentive bonus, paid time off, paid holidays, fitness reimbursement, company-provided phone, internet reimbursement, and reimbursed business travel and parking expense.
Invested in Your Growth: Build your career through ongoing training, mentorship, professional development opportunities, and a clear path to expand your expertise and take on greater responsibility.

Analyze intricate substantive and procedural legal and factual issues.
Conduct extensive, well-reasoned legal research.
Draft pleadings, dispositive motions ( e.g., motions for summary judgment, demurrers, motions to strike, etc.), discovery motions, discovery, and discovery responses.
Compile exhibits and review documents; prepare memoranda that analyze evidence and recommend next steps; find and coordinate with experts; conduct legal research and analysis; prepare trial documents, among other tasks.
Assist with trial preparation / possibly attend trial and participate in trial tasks.
Provide effective and timely communications, information, legal advice and other services to the senior attorneys on the complex litigation team, clients, and claims customers on legal and factual issues in a technology driven environment.
Communicate with court, witnesses, experts, opposing counsel, and co-counsel in a manner consistent with established office procedures.
May take depositions, appear in court, attend client and expert meetings and assist with mediation, arbitration and trial and may communicate with clients.
Apply strong legal research and writing skills, attention to detail, organization, strategic thinking, and collaboration to support complex litigation matters and deliver high-quality work across all aspects of your responsibilities.

Minimum of 3 years of legal practice experience handling tort defense matters.
Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited law school.
Domicile in California, active license to practice in California, and ability to appear in applicable local state and federal courts.
Member in good standing of California State Bar.
Strong legal research and writing skills (writing sample required).
Extensive experience writing substantive legal motions, including but not limited to motions for summary judgment and/or adjudication, demurrers and motions to strike.
Excellent organizational skills and ability to prioritize duties and time are a must.
Strong communication, computer and technology skills and the ability to quickly leverage new software are required.
Demonstrated expertise and familiarity in the handling of claim cases and litigation.

L'accent de cette position est mis sur la protection des droits de la propriété intellectuelle (droit des marques, design et droit d'auteur) y compris la lutte contre la contrefaçon/le marché gris. Vos atouts sont la persévérance, l'aptitude à négocier et une attitude positive face à vos tâches. Vous vous intéressez aux questions techniques et êtes curieux de découvrir de nouveaux domaines.
Vous travaillez de manière autonome et en équipe, vous avez le sens des responsabilités et vous vous caractérisez par votre grande volonté de fournir un service de qualité.
L'allemand, le français et l'anglais sont des langues que vous maîtrisez tant à l'oral qu'à l'écrit et dans lesquelles vous êtes capable de traiter des textes juridiques et de mener des négociations.

At Shakepay , we’re on a mission to usher in the Bitcoin golden age. We’re reimagining financial services to give every Canadian their fair shake.
Our culture is built around doing work that matters, winning as a team, and celebrating success. If you're the kind of person who values growth, shipping fast, and sharing your ideas openly with a group of like-minded people, come and build with us!
About Shakepay
Since 2015, we've been on a mission to help Canadians build long-term wealth through bitcoin.

Over the past few years, we've expanded beyond buying and selling bitcoin to offer a growing suite of everyday financial products - including the Shakepay Card, direct deposit, bill payments and Interac e-Transfer - making it easier to earn, save and use bitcoin every day.

Today, more than 1.5 million Canadians use Shakepay to grow their bitcoin savings and take control of their financial future as we continue to push the boundaries of what modern financial services can look like.
We’re regulated as an investment dealer across all Canadian provinces and territories, and backed by renowned venture capitalists with a funding of $44M. We have a passionate, loyal, and growing community, and we’re looking for people who want to help us build something truly special.

The Legal team sits at the center of some of Shakepay ’s most important decisions. We partner closely with Product, Compliance, Operations, Finance, People, and leadership to bring new products to market, navigate complex regulatory questions and help the business move quickly with confidence. We believe ownership over hierarchy, practical judgment over perfection, and using technology and AI to rethink how legal work gets done.

As Senior Legal Counsel, you’ll help shape how millions of Canadians interact with money. You’ll work alongside product, compliance and executive leadership to solve novel legal questions at the intersection of crypto, payments and financial regulation. This is a hands-on role for someone who can navigate ambiguity, provide practical recommendations and wants to help build - not just protect - the business.
What you’ll be doing
Partner with Product, Compliance and business teams to help design and launch new products, translating complex legal and regulatory requirements into practical solutions.
Advise on a broad range of legal and regulatory matters across securities, AML/ATF, payments, consumer protection and other areas impacting Shakepay 's business.
Lead regulatory initiatives, including supporting examinations, audits, licensing work, policy development and engagement with regulators.
Provide practical, business-oriented advice to leaders across the company, helping teams navigate ambiguity and make informed decisions while balancing legal, regulatory and operational considerations.
Identify opportunities to leverage AI, automation and scalable processes to improve how legal work gets done and enable the business to move faster.
Support the team on a variety of other legal matters as needed, including commercial agreements, corporate governance, employment and strategic projects.

Canadian-qualified lawyer with 5+ years of experience, ideally in fintech, payments, financial services, crypto, or a fast-moving technology company.
Able to operate independently in a lean team, make decisions with incomplete information, and move work forward without heavy oversight.
Business-oriented legal judgment: you start from the product or business outcome, then help the team understand risk, options, and a recommended path.
Comfortable advising product and operational teams directly, including on ambiguous questions where there may not be a perfect answer.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to turn complex legal issues into clear, practical guidance for non-legal stakeholders.

Experience working across both a law firm and an in-house legal team.
Experience in a startup or scaleup environment where priorities change quickly and legal support needs to be pragmatic.
Familiarity with Bitcoin, crypto, securities, payments, AML, or regulated financial products in Canada.
Experience using AI, automation, or lightweight tooling to improve legal work product and team efficiency.

Help shape the future of money: Be part of a team that's revolutionizing financial services in Canada, one sat at a time.
Impact millions: As cryptocurrency continues to gain traction, our potential for growth is massive. You can help us bring Shakepay and Bitcoin to all Canadians.
Grow your career: We’re growing, and so can you! We have programs in place to encourage continuous learning, growth, and development.
Ideas, not titles: We want the best ideas to make their way through, no matter where they come from.

🤝 Be an owner: Every employee has stock options as part of their total compensation.
🥅 Reach your goals: Develop with continuous feedback and quarterly performance and compensation review.
🦷 Health & wellness: Access to health and dental coverage, including health and wellness spending accounts.
🌎 Remote-friendly: Work from anywhere in Canada, with optional access to our office spaces in Montreal and Toronto.
🆙 Level Up: A $2,000 annual budget for courses, certifications, and training to support your career growth.
🌴 Time off: 20 days of vacation per year. And if you use all your vacation, we give you a $1,000 bonus.
🐣 Parental leave: Enjoy a parental leave top up to 100% of your salary for 18 weeks.
🙌 Have fun together: quarterly team-specific or company-wide offsite to connect with each other.
The base salary may vary based on factors such as years of experience, skills and qualifications. Additionally, employees are eligible for equity, pay increases based on performance, benefits including health and dental care, and paid time off.
We understand that potential can be just as valuable as experience. If you're eager to learn, grow, and contribute to the mission but worry that you may not have the “right” experience, we still want you to apply. We encourage applications from everyone, regardless of background and life experience. We’re firm believers that a little bit of slope makes up for a lot of y-intercept.

About Pair Team
Pair Team is a public benefit company reimagining care for the safety net. As an AI-enabled medical group for Medicaid and Medicare, we deliver medical, behavioral, and social care by integrating shelters, pantries and other community-based organizations into our whole-person model.

As California’s largest complex care provider, we’ve proven our impact to reduce avoidable emergency care, including a 52% and 26% reduction in ER visits and hospitalizations respectively. Once scaled nationally, our approach would save tax payers $150B per year.
With our years of experience and vast data collected, we are now building an AI platform that embeds social work agents across the safety net to truly unify our fragmented healthcare and welfare system. By scaling our country’s frontline medical and social services workforce, we aim to bring high-touch care to everyone.
At Pair Team , we’re not just delivering care—we’re transforming it. We’re building a future where high-touch, community-driven care is accessible to everyone, especially the most underserved.
Forbes: For Pair Team , Accessibility Is About Delivering Healthcare To Those Who Need It The Most
TechCrunch: Building for Medicaid’s regulatory moment with Neil Batlivala from Pair Team
Journal of General Internal Medicine: A Novel Intervention for Medicaid Beneficiaries with Complex Needs
About the Opportunity
We're hiring a Senior Legal Counsel to help Pair Team grow and scale responsibly. This is an opportunity to be the second lawyer in the legal department and build inside a fast-moving healthcare company operating at the center of Medicaid and Medicare high needs population care management.
This role reports directly to the Head of Legal.

Legal & Regulatory Guidance
Lead advisor on corporate, healthcare regulatory, litigation, commercial, product, employment, and privacy matters.
Monitor regulatory developments and translate their impact into clear, actionable guidance for product, clinical, and operations teams.
Collaborate with operational, clinical and marketing leaders to ensure adherence to applicable laws and regulations (e.g. HIPAA, Anti-Kickback, Corporate Practice of Medicine).
Understand and provide business friendly guidance on use and impact of artificial intelligence and other technologies in healthcare programs.
Commercial Strategy & Contracting
Work on contract development and negotiation—drafting, redlining, and advising on deal terms for health plans, vendors, and partners.
Draft templates and playbooks for contracting with partners, including service agreements, BAAs, NDAs, and other agreements..
Provide legal and regulatory guidance related to Medicaid, Medicare, value-based care, and product development to support commercial strategy.
Risk Identification & Building Out Legal Function
Act as a trusted advisor to business, product, and clinical teams — flagging legal risks early and helping design compliant solutions rather than blocking progress.
Help develop legal processes and policies that support risk mitigation, compliance, and business enablement.
Effectively manage outside counsel work and spend.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Partner with clinical operations on care delivery compliance, including documentation standards, authorization requirements, and billing compliance.
Collaborate with the People team on compliance training, onboarding, and workforce policy development.
Support company litigation needs.
Represent Pair Team professionally and compliantly in partner, health plan, and regulatory conversations.

What You’ll Need
5+ years of healthcare legal experience with direct exposure to federal programs (Medicare, Medicaid, or both) and the regulatory frameworks governing them (CMS, OIG, HIPAA, FWA).
3+ years legal experience at a digital health company, health plan, provider, or managed care organization operating in Medicaid and/or Medicare programs.
Demonstrated ability to operate in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment — startup or high-growth company experience strongly preferred.
Deep working knowledge of the healthcare regulatory environment and practical application to technology products and digital health services.
Strong communication skills — able to explain complex regulatory requirements in plain language and make crisp risk/benefit recommendations to business leaders.
Ability to multitask, prioritize, and manage projects and tasks.
Experience supporting building processes, procedures, and workflows that enable sustainable business scaling.
Strong collaboration skills with thought partners from clinical, operations, finance, and leadership
Proven ability to prioritize competing demands and make risk-proportionate decisions.
Mission-driven and passionate about improving outcomes for underserved communities

As a Attorney-Advisor (General) Open Continuous, GS-0905-13/14/15, your typical work assignments may include the following: Provides legal advice and counsel on extremely complex and difficult legal and policy issues affecting OA and EOP officials in the areas such as employment laws/personnel law, equal employment opportunity (EEO) laws, ethics and compliance, appropriations and fiscal law; procurement law; and security law (including such matters as personnel security and physical security).

Provides verbal and written advice and guidance to OA officials on legal issues, including statutes, regulations, directives, guidance and case law. Identifies legal issues, demonstrates an understanding of the role and mission of the EOP and OA, and effectively coordinates within OA and with other legal counterparts in EOP.

Drafts and reviews relevant documents and develops memoranda or other written responses from OA on legal matters. Analyzes and provides recommendations on proposed actions or approaches of projects that the OA is undertaking; explaining risks, legal considerations, and options to a variety of levels of staff and managers.

Provides briefings, presentations, and trainings to OA and EOP staff and senior officials on subjects required by law and others mandated by leadership.
ALL QUALIFICATIONS MUST BE MET BY THE CLOSING DATE OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. MINIMUM QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS: All applicants must meet the qualification requirements outlined below to be considered minimally qualified for this position. The qualification requirements are in accordance with the OPM Qualification Standards.

SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have a minimum of one year of specialized experience at a level of difficulty and responsibility comparable to the next lower grade or comparable pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private sector.

BASIC REQUIREMENTS: Applicants must meet one of the following criteria listed below in order to meet the basic requirement for Attorney-Advisor (General) Open Continuous, 0905.

Education: Applicants must possess a Bachelor of Law (LL.B), Master of Law (LL.M), or Juris Doctor (J.D.) law degree from a law school accredited by the American Bar Association (ABA).

(Must submit a copy of your transcripts with the degree conferred date, failure to do will result in an incomplete application.) Bar Membership: Applicants must be an active member in good standing with the bar of the highest court of a state, U.S. commonwealth, U.S. territory, or the District of Columbia, and must hold a current, unrestricted license to practice law.

AND You may qualify at the GS-13 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 grade level in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private sector that demonstrates conducting complex legal analysis and drafting legal documents as an attorney in one or more of the following practice areas: federal labor and employment law.

You may qualify at the GS-14 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private sector that demonstrates making recommendations on policies, analyzing and evaluating complex legal issues, and advising senior leadership on legal matters as an attorney in one or more of the following practice areas: federal labor and employment law.

* Collaborer avec les dirigeants commerciaux seniors pour soutenir les objectifs de croissance mondiale d'EPD en fournissant des conseils juridiques axés sur le commerce qui équilibrent opportunités commerciales et gestion appropriée des risques.
* Diriger le soutien juridique pour des transactions stratégiques importantes, y compris les licences, acquisitions, cessions, gestion des alliances, accords de chaîne d'approvisionnement, transactions de fabrication et autres accords commerciaux complexes.
* Fournir un leadership juridique pour les activités de développement commercial d'EPD, y compris la structuration des transactions, la diligence raisonnable, la négociation, la planification de l'intégration et la gouvernance continue des alliances.
* Conseiller les organisations Opérations et Chaîne d'Approvisionnement Globale d'EPD sur la fabrication, les achats, la continuité de l'approvisionnement, la qualité, le transfert de technologie, le développement pharmaceutique et les accords commerciaux avec des tiers.
* Identifier, évaluer et gérer de manière proactive les risques juridiques, réglementaires, de conformité et de réputation affectant les opérations mondiales et les priorités stratégiques d'EPD.
* Négocier, rédiger et superviser un large éventail d'accords commerciaux complexes et établir des normes, processus et meilleures pratiques contractuelles à travers la division.
* Représenter la Division Juridique dans les comités de gouvernance clés, les forums de direction et les initiatives transversales, fournissant des conseils stratégiques sur les décisions commerciales critiques.

* Développer et dispenser des formations juridiques, des orientations et des outils pratiques qui favorisent des pratiques commerciales conformes et soutiennent une prise de décision efficace dans toute l'EPD.
